business: Wukong (a competitive work marketplace where the buyer locks a reward and an AI judge scores the entries)
by_segment: Web3 project ops or community manager
Marketing or content lead at an SMB or agency
Community, event or education organiser (career centre, conference, nonprofit)
Startup or small-team founder / ops lead
by_behaviour: Hires a freelancer they already trust
Asks for a sample, reads reviews
why_not: I can't tell who is behind this or whether it's legitimate, and I'd have to explain a crypto payment to whoever signs off on my budget. My first move is to ask ChatGPT or Claude for the draft anyway, and I only pay a person if that isn't good enough.

I go to a freelancer I already trust, and I answer for every dollar. Locking money in a contract on a brand-new, unaudited product isn't something I'd explain to my boss. Winner-takes-all also means I pay 55 USDC and might get nothing usable.

I have a freelancer I already trust and I'm not moving a nonprofit's money onto a new platform that nobody has audited. I'd also have to explain USDC on Solana to my finance person, and that alone kills it.

My backlog is small copy and translation jobs, and I just ask Claude for a draft and fix it myself. Paying 55 USDC for a contest where most entries get nothing feels like spec work, and I'm not sending money to an unaudited new product.

I won't set up a wallet or hold USDC for a business purchase, and that rules it out before I even look at the rest. Even if it were in dollars, writing a rubric for every task is extra work and I can get a first draft from a model for free.
I don't do crypto. I'm not setting up a Solana wallet or holding USDC to pay for a 50 dollar task, and I'd have to explain that to whoever signs off on my spend.

For a 50 USDC task I would just ask Claude for the draft and only pay a person if it came back bad. 55 USDC with only the top entries paid, plus USDC on Solana, is more hassle and money than a small task is worth to me.

55 USDC for a small task I could get a first draft of from a model for free, and only the top entries get paid so I might get nothing usable for it. I'm budget-tight and want to see a sample first, and this is unaudited, invitation-only and needs USDC on Solana.
why_yes: The free pilot is the hook: I like trying new tools and one small task costs me nothing. I would not pay the 55 USDC after that unless the free run showed me something clearly better than a model draft.
I like trying new tools and the first task is free, so I'd run one small pilot for fun. I wouldn't pay for a second one until I'd seen what came back.
I like trying new tools and the first task is free with the founder helping, so I would run one small pilot for fun. I would not put real money in until I have seen how the judge scores things.

I'd take the free pilot task because it costs me nothing and I like trying new tools. I wouldn't pay real money for a second one until I've seen how the judge scores and whether the winning entry is actually usable.

I always have a pile of small translation and content jobs, and a free first task is a cheap way to try something new. I'd run one pilot for fun, but I'm not committing real budget until I see how it goes.
flip: Named founders I can verify, a few real nonprofit or education customers I can contact, and a way to pay by card or invoice instead of USDC. The free trial task would help, but only once I can tell the company is real.

A referral from someone I trust who has used it, plus an independent audit, and a way to pay by card so I don't have to handle USDC. The free first task would also have to cost me nothing in real money.
A free trial where I see real entries judged against my rubric and the winning one clearly beats what Claude gives me, plus a way to pay by card and a reference from another organiser who used it.
Let me pay by card or invoice in dollars, with a ready-made rubric template so I don't have to write one from scratch.
Pay by card or invoice instead of USDC, plus a reference from another organisation like mine that has used it, with the free trial task run for me so there is no risk.
An independent audit, plus a free first task where I can see the AI judge's scores and reasons on real entries and they beat what I get from Claude in ten minutes.
